tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

2	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
3	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
8	  modified: 2026-09-18T23:28:33.951Z
9	---
10	
11	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
12	
13	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
14	
15	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
16	
17	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
18	
19	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
20	
21	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
22	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
23	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
24	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
25	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
26	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
27	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
28	the harness had opened on the Acer.
29	
30	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
31	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
32	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
33	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
34	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
35	
36	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
37	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
38	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
39	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
40	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
41	concluding anything about the app.
42	
43	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
44	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
45	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
46	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
47	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
48	
49	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
50	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:28:33.951Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

---
name: add-printer-flow-figma-discrepancy
description: "Add Printer Flow verified against Figma (2026-09-13): 18f matches closely, but 'Set it up myself' opens the stock Orca ConfigWizard, not the Figma-designed 18e grid"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 39ab79c2-8166-4a6c-aab4-90964465ffbd
  modified: 2026-09-13T22:15:58.423Z
---

Verified the JusPrin v2 Figma file's "Add Printer Flow" page
(https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2, frames
18a-18f) against the running app on 2026-09-13, on the
figma-design-file-42aa00 worktree rebased onto
claude/add-printer-flow-changes-d2e0fa (commit cb5fe93e05 "Apply the Add
Printer Flow Figma changes to the dialog").

**Matches well:** 18f "No agent connected" state — text, layout, icon,
button, and the "Or **set it up myself** from the lists" footer are a close
match to Figma. "Set up the agent" correctly routes to the Agent Setup
empty-state page per Figma's cross-page note.

**Confirmed discrepancy:** the "set it up myself" link does NOT open the
Figma-designed 18e screen (a scoped grid of just Bambu Lab models, with a
Printer/Filaments/Bed shape/Firmware sidebar and an "Ask the agent instead"
link, inside the same "Add a printer" modal chrome). Instead it opens Orca's
stock `ConfigWizard` "Printer Selection" page — the same generic
all-vendors grid (Klipper, Marlin, RepRap, Afinia, ...) shown in the
first-run Setup Wizard, with plain Confirm/Create/Cancel buttons and no
scoping or "Ask the agent instead" link. Confirmed both by code
(`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:338`/`:401` calls Orca's own `ConfigWizard`) and by
driving the real app.

**Not independently visually verified this pass:** 18a (Initial evidence
entry), 18b (Recognized), 18c (Network Selected), 18d (Ambiguous) — these
need either a live configured OpenAI agent or a real discovered network
printer, neither available in the sandboxed test environment. Code
(`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:471,702`) has these states named to match the Figma
frame numbers, suggesting intentional alignment, but this wasn't visually
confirmed. `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp --printer-setup` (via
`open_printer_setup_with` fixtures) is the deterministic way to reach these
states without live network/API dependencies — worth using for full
coverage.

**How to reproduce the live check:** ditto the built `.app`, replace
`CFBundleIdentifier`, ad-hoc codesign, launch with a scratch
`--datadir` and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` (lands cleanly on 18f without live
network calls). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] for the general recipe.
computer-use's `request_access` was denied on the first attempt (likely an
unattended auto-deny) and granted on retry — don't assume denial is final,
but don't hammer retries either; ask the user first.

Related: [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]], [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]].

The app is running (pid 62686) — check your screen for the JusPrin window.

What this branch changes, so you know what to try: in Home, click "Add Printer" — the printer setup conversation panel should now take over the entire workspace (hiding the 3D/print content behind it) instead of sitting in a narrow side column. If you instead open settings for an **existing** printer, it should still use the narrower side-panel layout next to Home, unchanged from before.

A couple of notes on how I set this up:
- I fetched `codex/focused-printer-setup` from `origin` and built it in its own git worktree at [.claude/worktrees/codex-focused-printer-setup](.claude/worktrees/codex-focused-printer-setup) — your `jusprin-newui` checkout wasn't touched.
- I copied the built app to a scratch location and gave it a distinct bundle id (`com.jusprin.codex-focused-printer-setup`) so it won't collide with any other JusPrin/OrcaSlicer instance you might have running.
- It's using your real JusPrin data directory (printers, projects, settings), not a scratch one — let me know if you'd rather I relaunch it against an isolated profile instead.
